# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-34 (Extended v219)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to summer Year 9. Key Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Champs-Élysées, Rue Saint-Honoré, Luxembourg Garden, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Temple, sewers (Sainte-Avoye, Louvre, Montmartre, belt, Amelot, Beautreillis), Marais, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons, Saint-Paul church, Rue Beautreillis near Arsenal, Grand Sewer, Rue de l'Hôpital. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Wilholt, Torton, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Gulhaven.

## English Subplot Summary

**Established facts through summer Year 9**: Multiple residents migrated between villages. **NEW (Chapter 34): Semor swore to Isric Thornmere to rebuild the fallen wall at Kelmere, shook on it.** Solemn promises: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven; Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard above Salcombe (summer Year 7); Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard above Wilholt (autumn Year 7); Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair chapel roof at Kelmere (winter Year 8); Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest; Kassa's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe.

**Chapter 33 domestic observations**: Pelde Stenson, Dalis Stenworth, Davus, Rimor Corrford, Kassa Brackick, Volan Stenworth tired or aching. Yera Stenworth sorted old letters, hummed tune while scrubbing step, read almanac mispronouncing saints. Istho Stenworth hummed tune while scrubbing step, counted coins twice (came up penny short), asked if it would rain (Isric shrugged). Luvie Prydenridge bought ribbon (regretted it), hummed tune while scrubbing step, discussed salt prices scandal. Istho, Jotho, Nerine predicted rain (wrongly). Jotho mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Rozek Stenenridge fell asleep before fire. Lurald remarked river up; Yera said it always was in spring. Luvie told Rozek old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. Luvie and Semor Brackick argued with carter over oats price. Smoke lay flat; gulls quarreled over fish heads. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Rain threatened but held off. Baker's boy late. Bells rang thinly. Children chased hoop. Salt prices discussed as scandalous. Kassa counted coins twice (came up penny short). Only son of Luena Stenenridge packed single trunk, moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven.

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship to Death Vigil

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed orphan status, lawyer profession, father colonel-hero. Cosette revealed convent upbringing, dead mother, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (June Year 6)**: Éponine died leading Marius to barricade. Marius witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery (7 September)**: Doctor declared recovery assured. When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; another Fauchelevent was real father. **Dowry: five hundred eighty thousand francs, constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.** Gillenormand overwhelmed her with gifts.

**Wedding (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent injured hand paining him; begged excuse; would come tomorrow. Jean Valjean rose, left unperceived during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis post-wedding**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets, pillow without case. All feminine objects removed. Only Jean Valjean's bed made up. Remained twelve long hours ice-cold, motionless as corpse. Then shuddered convulsively, kissed Cosette's garments.

**Javert's death (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed on quay edge. Tall black figure appeared on parapet, bent towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down. Dull splash followed. Javert drowned. **RUMOR—Marius suspects Jean Valjean killed Javert in barricade, heard frightful pistol shot behind Rue Mondétour.**

**Jean Valjean's revelation and estrangement (17 February morning)**:
Very pale, eyes hollow, sunken by sleeplessness. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Justified: conscience implacable; duty places one in hell. Marius shocked, pleaded with him not to tell Cosette: "She does not know, it would terrify her."

Jean Valjean chose to tell himself—nothing forced him. If police arrived, exposed through own act. **Marius's doubt: questioned whether failed in divining Jean Valjean's nature. Reflected on six-seven ecstatic weeks in Rue Plumet, never spoke to Cosette of Gorbeau hovel or Thénardiers. Concluded: even had discovered Jean Valjean convict, would not have changed him or Cosette. Nothing to regret.**

**Marius's metaphysical rationalization**: God visible in affair. Jean Valjean horrible workman but admirable work. Dung-heap aids spring to create rose. Adored Cosette, possessed her, she splendidly pure. Cosette is light. Jean Valjean is empty chrysalis.

**Marius's final position**: Convict appeared hideous, repulsive. Not examined right man takes to dispose of irrevocable. Not shocked by vengeance. Weakness led to imprudent concession; promised Jean Valjean; must keep word. First duty to Cosette. Acquired mysterious information about six hundred thousand francs without seeking it. Unable to probe out of respect for promised secret. Believed grave duty: restitution to someone sought with discretion. Abstained from touching money meanwhile.

**Cosette's alienation**: Address as _thou_ replaced by _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean," rendering him another person. She became more gay, less tender. Still loved him sincerely. One day chanced to say "father." Flash of joy illuminated his melancholy countenance. He caught her up: "Say Jean."—"Ah! truly, Monsieur Jean," she replied with laughter. **"That is right," said he. Turned aside to wipe eyes. This was the last time.** Complete extinction ensued. No more familiarity, no more good-morning with kiss. After losing Cosette wholly in one day, afterwards obliged to lose her again in detail.

**Marius's estrangement strategy**: Before marriage, put no questions to M. Fauchelevent; since marriage, feared to put any to Jean Valjean. Regretted promise. Confined himself to gradually estranging Jean Valjean from house and effacing him from Cosette's mind. Always placed himself between them. More than effacement, it was eclipse.

**Cosette's magnetism**: All-powerful magnetism causing her to do instinctively what Marius wished. Conscious of Marius' will regarding "Monsieur Jean," she conformed to it. Her obedience consisted in not remembering what Marius forgot. Soul became wholly husband's; which was shrouded in gloom in Marius' mind became overcast in hers. **Concerning Jean Valjean, this forgetfulness was merely superficial. Rather heedless than forgetful. At bottom, sincerely attached to man whom so long called her father; but loved her husband still more dearly. This had somewhat disturbed balance of her heart, which leaned to one side only.**

**Jean Valjean's withdrawal (late spring/summer 1833)**: Old man neatly clad in black emerged daily at same hour towards nightfall from Rue de l'Homme Armé. Passed Blancs-Manteaux, gained Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, reached Rue de l'Écharpe, turned left into Rue Saint-Louis. Soon went only as far as Rue Pavée, shook head, turned back. Then did not overstep Blancs-Manteaux. Whole countenance expressed single idea: What is use? Eye dim, no radiance. Tears exhausted. Head craned forward; chin moved; folds in gaunt neck painful to behold. Sometimes had umbrella but never opened it. **A week passed: Jean Valjean had not taken a step in his room, remained in bed. Portress said old man does not get up, no longer eats, will not last long; his daughter made bad marriage. One evening found difficulty raising himself on elbow; felt wrist, could not find pulse; breath short, halted at times; recognized he was weaker than ever before. Made effort, drew himself up into sitting posture, dressed in old workingman's clothes. Obliged to pause many times; putting arms through waistcoat made perspiration trickle from forehead. One day descended staircase, took three steps in street, seated himself on post; remained few moments, went upstairs. This was last oscillation of pendulum. Following day did not leave apartment. Day after that, did not leave bed.**

**Physical deterioration**: **He was eighty years old; before Marius' marriage, would have hardly been taken for fifty; that year had counted for thirty.** What he bore on brow was no longer wrinkles of age, but mysterious mark of death. Hollowing of that pitiless nail could be felt there. Cheeks pendulous; skin had color leading one to think earth already upon it; corners of mouth drooped as in mask ancients sculptured on tombs. Gazed into space with air of reproach; grand tragic being who had cause to complain of someone.

**Preparations for death**: Took Bishop's candlesticks from chimney-piece, took two wax candles from drawer, put them in candlesticks. Lighted them though broad daylight, summer time. Forced to rise and put few drops of water in ink. Compelled to write with back of pen. Wiped brow. **[Lamentable cries heard by God alone]: "All is over. I shall never see her more. She is a smile which passed over me. I am about to plunge into night without even seeing her again. Oh! one minute, one instant, to hear her voice, to touch her dress, to gaze upon her, the angel! and then to die! What is frightful is to die without seeing her. She would smile on me, she would say a word to me. Here I am all alone. My God! My God! I shall never see her again!"**

## Thénardier's Blackmail Attempt and Marius's Confrontation

**Thénardier's discovery and visit**: Through daughter Azelma tracking married pair and personal researches, Thénardier discovered Cosette was Madame la Baronne Pontmercy. Discovered man encountered in Grand Sewer. Knew Cosette's identity but meant to be discreet. Caught inkling of illegitimacy but judged insufficient leverage; had better wares. Feared revealing bastard status would only result in being kicked out. Wore black cloth coat, silk waistcoat, boots, linen, green glasses, plastered gray hair, hat in hand, bent attitude, bunch of seals from fob. **Offered to drive individual from family who has no right there; claimed Madame la Baronne of lofty birth; sanctuary of virtue cannot cohabit longer with crime. Demanded twenty thousand francs.** Marius replied with cold tone, double "I know it," laconicism not favorable to dialogue.

**Thénardier's exposure**: With agility of monkey, tore off spectacles, withdrew two quills from nose, took off face as man takes off hat. **Strangely surprised; would have been troubled, had he capable of such a thing. Had come to bring astonishment, received it instead. This humiliation worth five hundred francs to him, accepted it; but bewildered nonetheless.** Despite disguise, Baron recognized him thoroughly. Thénardier never seen Marius before.

**Marius's knowledge**: **Revealed Javert's suicide facts**: Announced two newspapers: _Moniteur_ of 15th June, 1832, announced Javert's suicide, adding that Javert reported to prefect that, having been taken prisoner in barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie, he owed his life to magnanimity of insurgent who, holding him under pistol, fired into air instead of blowing out his brains. **Marius possessed evidence, certain date, irrefragable proof. Could not doubt.**

Marius felt humiliated that colonel-hero should have owed anything to Thénardier. Thénardier's letter of change drawn from tomb by Marius' father, protested up to that day. Seemed occasion to avenge Colonel for misfortune of being saved by rascal. By side of this duty lay another: to elucidate, if possible, source of Cosette's fortune.

**Marius's confrontation speech**: **Told Thénardier: "You are an infamous wretch! you are a liar, a calumniator, a villain. You came to accuse that man, you have only justified him; you wanted to ruin him, you have only succeeded in glorifying him. And it is you who are the thief! And it is you who are the assassin! I saw you, Thénardier Jondrette, in that lair on the Rue de l'Hôpital. I know enough about you to send you to the galleys and even further if I choose. Here are a thousand francs, bully that you are! Of a Colonel! I wouldn't give a ha'penny for a general. And you come here to commit infamies! I tell you that you have committed all crimes. Go! disappear! Only be happy, that is all that I desire. Ah! monster! here are three thousand francs more. Take them. You will depart to-morrow, for America, with your daughter; for your wife is dead, you abominable liar. I shall watch over your departure, you ruffian, and at that moment I will count out to you twenty thousand francs. Go get yourself hung elsewhere!"**

**Thénardier's outcome**: **The moral wretchedness of Thénardier was irremediable. He was in America what he had been in Europe. With Marius' money, Thénardier set up as slave-dealer.**

## Jean Valjean's Reconciliation and Final Vigil (Chapter 34)

**Marius and Cosette's discovery of Jean Valjean's deterioration**: By accident, Marius learned all Jean Valjean had done. Told Jean Valjean: "Your chamber still stands ready in our house." Insisted Jean Valjean part of themselves; he is Cosette's father and Marius's. Shall not pass another day in dreadful house. Not imagining he will be there tomorrow.

**Cosette's invitation**: "If you only knew how pretty the garden is now! The azaleas are doing very well there. The walks are sanded with river sand; there are tiny violet shells. You shall eat my strawberries. I water them myself. And no more 'madame,' no more 'Monsieur Jean,' we are living under a Republic, everybody says _thou_, don't they, Marius? The programme is changed. If you only knew, father, I have had a sorrow, there was a robin redbreast which had made her nest in a hole in the wall, and a horrible cat ate her. My poor, pretty, little robin red-breast which used to put her head out of her window and look at me! I cried over it. I should have liked to kill the cat. But now nobody cries any more. Everybody laughs, everybody is happy. You are going to come with us. How delighted grandfather will be! You shall have your plot in the garden, you shall cultivate it, and we shall see whether your strawberries are as fine as mine. And, then, I shall do everything that you wish, and then, you will obey me prettily."

**Jean Valjean's response to their plea**: **Claims Death is good arrangement; God knows better what we need. May Marius have Cosette, may youth wed morning, may lilacs and nightingales surround them, may life be beautiful sunny lawn. Now let him die; all is right. Last night drank whole jug of water. Cosette much better off with husband. "Even if you were to take possession of me, Monsieur Pontmercy, would that make me other than I am? No, God has thought like you and myself, and he does not change his mind; it is useful for me to go."**

**Final strength and gesture**: **All at once rose to his feet. These accesses of strength are sometimes sign of death agony. Walked with firm step to wall, thrusting aside Marius and doctor who tried to help him, detached from wall little copper crucifix suspended there, returned to seat with freedom of movement of perfect health, laid crucifix on table, spoke in loud voice.**
